steps.text: Whisk eggs, milk, water, and salt together in a large mixing bowl. Add flour and melted butter; whisk vigorously until batter is smooth and pourable.

Heat a lightly oiled griddle or frying pan over medium-high heat. Pour or scoop the batter onto the pan, using approximately 1/4 cup for each crêpe. Tilt the pan with a circular motion so that the batter coats the surface evenly.

Cook until the top of the crêpe is no longer wet and the bottom has turned light brown, 1 to 2 minutes. Run a spatula around the edge of the skillet to loosen the crêpe; flip and cook until the other side has turned light brown, about 1 minute more.

raw_recipe.headline: Basic Crêpes
raw_recipe.description: This crêpe recipe uses simple pantry ingredients to make delicious French-style pancakes. Perfect for brunch with a sweet or savory filling!

video.description: Enjoy a European-style brunch in under 30 minutes with these delicious crepes. In this video, the Allrecipes team shows you how to quickly make basic crepes over the stove using easily available ingredients! Similar in appearance to pancakes, crepes are comprised of a flour mixture that only uses five ingredients. Pour the mixture into a pan over the stove and cook until lightly browned. With powdered sugar, fresh fruit, and a dollop of whipped cream, enjoy this light and sweet start to your day.

review.reviewBody: Great recipe, with ONE exception: I initially followed the directions to whisk the flour/eggs then add the wet ingredients, but this left me with VERY lumpy unusable batter. Doing the reverse - mixing the eggs & wet stuff then sifting in the flour - worked way better.

BRILLIANT BASIC CREPES.
This is a scrumptious recipe for thin, delicious German style pancakes. I'm a professional musician and recording artist, and I often find myself in the kitchens of recording studios, trying to make something edible from the staple ingredients studios keep in their kitchens. Well, this recipe is it!!! Everyone has milk, eggs, salt, butter, and flour in their kitchen, and these babies whip up like a charm! Even the batter will keep in the fridge for a few days. Personally, I like to throw in about a third cup of granulated sugar and a quarter cup of powdered sugar to make them sweet and a little crispy around the edges. Just be sure to put a fresh dab of butter in the pan before pouring the batter each time. I've tried countless pancake/crepe recipes, and nothing really impressed me until this one. I recommend it most enthusiastically!

Christine Anderson

I made these last night for my kids and I because I just came home from Paris. They were a huge hit! I gently scraped the excess batter off the top towards the edges just like they do in France, and it made them thinner and just the right consistency with perfect browning and rolling capabilities. I added some lemon juice and sugar to one kid's, salted caramel to another, nutella to my youngest's, and chestnut cream to mine and I felt like it was an amazing first attempt at crepes! To get rid of lumps I just pressed the lumps open to the side as best as I could. The final product didn't have any flour pockets, so it worked out I think.

This is easy and turns out awesome. I did mix and whisk the eggs, milk, water and slightly less salt (than the recommended 2 teaspoons) together first, then added the flour and melted butter and whisked it in, until the batter was smooth. Makes 4-5 crepes, as specified.

This crepe batter is really, really good! I mixed the dry ingredients in my stand mixer with the whisk attachment, then poured in the milk, water, & 1/2 t. of vanilla all at once, mixed it well, and then added the eggs and mixed well again. It blended wonderfully and I only had a few tiny specks that didn't mix that were settled at the bottom of the bowl when I was done pouring & making them. I did take another reviewers advice on adding the vanilla and 1/3 c. of sugar, but it was a tiny bit too sweet after we put our strawberry filling inside and the sweetened whip cream on top. They were so good I decided to make more for the next day and some to freeze, so I made the recipe again, doubling it, and only used the 1/3 c. for both instead of each, and that was perfect for us. These were great! :) (I just wish they were faster to cook! lol)

This is a great recipe! Followed it exactly but added a little bit of vanilla and mixed it very well in a blender. Consistency was perfect. Cooked them on my Blackstone Grille with a little wooden crepe tool and the grille surface temp at around 400 degrees F. Tripled the recipe and it fed 5 adults and 6 kids.

I bring my milk and eggs to room temp, add a dash of vanilla and a tbs of sugar since we eat them sweet. Using a hand blender I slowly sift the dry into the wet and then pour it all through a mesh sieve. Wrap tightly and place in fridge for an hour before cooking 🥰

This was the first time for me making crepes. I used a blender to blend all the wet ingredients thoroughly. Then, I poured it into a big bowl and whisked in the flour I sifted in while whisking. No lumps at all. Then I whisked in the melted butter at the end. I added a little extra melted butter, salt, sugar and vanilla. I heated the Rock crepe pan to medium high, used a brush the spread a small nob of butter on the pan. I held the pan off the element while pouring the batter and swirling the pan as I poured the batter to level it out in a circle. I discovered that doing it that way helped the batter to spread evenly and not mound up thicker in the middle like it did when I left the pan on the element. I just squeezed fresh lemon and maple syrup on them and they were delicious. Thank you!

The batter came out a bit thick, following the directions, but I tripped the recipe (feeding 4 boys) so that may have been a scaling thing. Added about another cup of water and it thined to the right consistency. Flavor and texture when cooked was spot-on, though, and exactly what I wanted. Good eggy flavor and just enough chew!

This recipe was perfect. My first crêpe recipe that reminds me of the delicious crêpes I had in Paris. The only thing I added was a little vanilla extract to the batter. I made a fruit compote in a sauce pan, consisting of fresh raspberries, blackberries and strawberries. They’re all in season so they’re all inexpensive at Costco right now. You just put the fruit in a sauce pan and let them boil down. don’t need to add any water or anything because you’ll get it from the fruit and then add about a cup to a cup and a half of sugar And continue to let that boil. We topped the crêpes with fresh whip whipped cream. My daughter doesn’t like fruit so I made her filling out of chocolate chips and bananas, and some Nutella topped again with whipped cream. The whole family loved these I made the recipe times four so I have plenty for the week and will probably at one point make savory as well as sweet crêpes. This is a perfect base recipe for any type of crêpe. Way way better in my opinion than the buckwheat crêpes that they serve in restaurants. Those are gross to me. Huge thank you for the recipe.!!!!

I really liked this recipes for a simple beginner recipe, however i found that the batter was too think so I had to add about half a cup more water (I also used coconut milk instead of regular milk, but the consistency was about the same as whole milk so i knew I'd have to compensate a little). Aside from needing a bit of extra water though, this recipe was awesome and I'd definitely use it again as a base recipe for adding to. Wonderful!
Simple and effective. Makes great crepes.
Perfect!
These crepes come out perfect. My favorite is serve hot with peanut butter and banana.
just add the vanilla
Important step is to let batter rest for and hour. My French friend told me this after I asked her why her crepes come out better than mine.
so good

Crepes were rather thick and kind of rubbery in the original recipe. Here’s what I did: Same recipe for (1/2x) but use extra 1/4 cup milk. Note: this will make a thinner batter, which is what I wanted as well, and this will increase the total volume of the batter. I’ve gotten 6 crepes out of that modification. I just put leftover batter in a container in the fridge.
yes

I think this recipe is great, I recommend making sure your pan is not too hot before pouring in the batter so that it doesn't congeal too quickly. I also like how it is ambiguous, I am able to put in sweet and savory fillings. I made a crepe with egg, cheese, and some hot sauce on top.
